knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to identify touchpoints by actual site use, clean along a planned route and use fresh tools or approved reprocessing between zones. Identifying touchpoints from site use and routing to avoid moving contamination from sanitary to cleaner areas is the correct check; sharing one mop head across a bathroom and a kitchen is not.

Stopping, isolating the affected equipment and escalating under the site procedure is the correct response to an uncontrolled hazard. Continuing to use the equipment, asking the client whether they mind the risk, or spraying an electrical device all leave the hazard live or create a new one.
The instruction says to use fresh tools or an approved reprocessing method between zones and tasks.

practicalCriteria: Follows the authorised sequence and site procedures
Uses suitable tools, product instructions and contamination controls
Recognises and escalates unsafe or out-of-scope conditions
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 4: Keep used mop heads and cloths separate from clean stock, and do not use one mop head for a bathroom and a kitchen.
Record of procedure step 8: Record the work completed and any inaccessible surfaces.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 4 is not done: Keep used mop heads and cloths separate from clean stock, and do not use one mop head for a bathroom and a kitchen.
Stop work if procedure step 5 is not done: Do not spray liquids directly onto electrical devices unless the manufacturer authorises the method.
